title: AI Citation Ready Blog Optimization Checklist
body_markdown:
# AI Citation Ready Blog Optimization Checklist

An AI citation ready blog gives readers a direct answer, shows who is responsible for the advice, and backs current search claims with dated sources.

## AI citation ready blog sections

AI citation ready blog sections should open with a compact answer that names the entity, the task, and the evidence source in one place.

Teams can then add examples, screenshots, or editorial notes after the first paragraph. In our data review example, the editor checks whether each section can be lifted as a standalone answer without losing context.

## Article schema and visible entities

Article schema should match visible page facts such as headline, author, publisher, dates, and the canonical URL.

The schema is not a separate promise of ranking performance. It supports machine understanding when the visible content already helps readers.

## E-E-A-T review notes

The review should identify the author, state when the article was updated, and explain why the team is qualified to make the recommendation.

This checklist links to Google guidance on helpful content and AI features so reviewers can verify the advice before publishing. See [Google helpful content guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) and [Google AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features).
